chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Among the most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is satisfying the hunger of the believer, or relieving his distress, or paying off his debt.
ai.seo_question: What are the most beloved deeds to God according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates practical social welfare—specifically feeding the hungry, relieving distress, and settling debts—to the status of beloved acts of worship. In Shia scholarship, these three acts are often viewed as comprehensive remedies for both material and spiritual hardships, reinforcing the communal responsibility (haqq al-nas) towards fellow believers. This narration underscores that tangible assistance is not merely charity but a means of drawing closer to Allah through service to His creation.
